chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A Makkan person should not lead the pilgrimage season.

key_terms.يَلِي: To lead, preside over, or take charge of

ai.seo_question: Who should lead the Hajj pilgrimage according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a specific legal ruling regarding the leadership of the Hajj pilgrimage season (al-Mawsim), stating that a native of Mecca (Makki) should not preside over the pilgrims. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted to prevent local tribal influence or bias from dominating the religious rites, ensuring the Imam or appointed leader maintains impartial authority over the diverse body of pilgrims. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholarly network in preserving this administrative guideline for the Hajj.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘No Makkan person should lead the pilgrims’.
en.sarwar: 12. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-FIassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “This is a Hadith of Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘
Residents of Makkah must not be appointed as waliy (the person in charge of the affairs of the pilgrims) of the people performing al-Hajj.’”
